All reasonable expenses incurred by the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in connection with (i) the transition of servicing rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer and (ii) amending this Agreement or entering into an assumption agreement or new agreement to reflect a succession of the Servicer will be paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer on receipt of an invoice in reasonable detail.</quote>
<parameter name="rationale">The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/termination fee payable by us (the Issuer or Depositor) to Cellco — full-text searches for "liquidated damages" and "penalty" return nothing, and the only amounts we owe the counterparty are ordinary compensation for services actually rendered (Servicing Fee at 0.75%, Supplemental Servicing Fee, Temporarily Excluded Receivables Servicing Fee under p0134). This meets the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages. We reviewed the planner's candidates: (i) the $150,000 appointment fee and the Additional Successor Servicer Fee (excess of $425,000 over the Servicing Fee, p0570) are compensation to a third-party Successor Servicer for work performed after Cellco resigns or is removed, not a penalty running to the counterparty, and the correlative transition expenses are pushed onto the resigning or terminated Servicer under Section 7.5(c) — a term that benefits us; and (ii) the Make-Whole Payment is yield maintenance payable to Noteholders on an Issuer-elected Optional Redemption (p0358), not a breach-triggered charge payable to the counterparty, and it is expressly excluded on a Clean-Up Redemption (p0351). Both fall outside this rule's direction test, so no redline is required.
